newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin appeals for accord in Nagorno-Karabakh.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin appeals for accord in Nagorno-Karabakh.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin appealed to Armenia and Azerbaijan on Monday to speed up efforts to solve the territorial dispute over the Nagorno-Karabakh enclave and offered Russian help in the process.

Yeltsin issued his appeal to mark the third anniversary of a 1994 ceasefire which ended the worst fighting but found no political solution and has not prevented sporadic clashes since then, including in the past few weeks.
"The military conflict has not been wiped out. The suffering continues for hundreds of thousands of people who left their homes," Yeltsin said in a statement released by the Kremlin.
It was addressed to the presidents of Armenia and Azerbaijan and the leader of Nagorno-Karabakh.

"I want to take this opportunity to make an insistent appeal to all leaders of all sides in the conflict to focus attention on the key questions of a settlement, the solving of which open the way to immediate agreement and the signing of a political accord."
Christian Armenians and Moslem Azeris went to war in the late 1980s over Nagorno-Karabakh, which was mainly populated by Armenians despite being inside Azerbaijan's borders.
The fighting killed thousands of people in the first major ethnic conflict in the former Soviet Union.
Yeltsin offered Russia's help, including arranging top-level meetings, to Armenian President Levon Ter-Petrosyan, Azerbaijan President Haydar Aliyev and Nagorno-Karabakh leader Leonard Petrosyan.

He said issues to be addressed included the creation of conditions for ensuring Azerbaijan's territorial integrity, the return of refugees and displaced persons, and guarantees of Nagorno-Karabakh's security and links with the outside world.
Despite the end of the war, Azerbaijan and Armenia accused each last month of staging cross-border attacks in what was the worst fighting since the two countries signed the ceasefire.
